units.translation: [Sept. 206 ἀΰπνων [sleepless] is a corruption for ἄπυον [without a cry]. See ἠπύω [to call].
standing upright, sleepless, not bending the knee.
where I restored αὔρας [breezes] for ἀπλοίας [lack of sailing], which is read in M from a gloss.
he sailed by the breeze of the giant Zephyrus.
wandering in wide (these words are corrupt) breezes.
long-lasting breezes that hold ships back,

αὐριβάτας [swift-footed]: Aeschylus uses αὖρι [tomorrow] (thus for αὔριον [tomorrow] Pauw; τὸ αὐρί [the word αὖρι] Toup) for 'quickly'. And the same author in Psychostasia (fr. 278) uses the word thus. ταχυβήμων [swift-stepping] (thus for ταχυβήλων [swift-throwing] Salmasius).
αὐρίβατον [swift-footed]: they use αὖρι [tomorrow] for 'quickly', and perhaps not from αὔρα [breeze], but according to some barbarian word. Perhaps also from αὔριον [tomorrow].

where Hermann reads οἰδματόεντ' ἀμφίδρομον | πόρον, εἰς μ [swelling, running-around passage, into...] etc. More probably R. Ellis in The Philological Journal, Cambridge 1868 vol. 1 p. 71) reads οἰδματόεντ' αὐρίδρομον πόρον συθείς [having rushed through the swelling, swift-running passage], except that he should rather have written αὐρίδρομος [swift-running].

a cup, in which (the Sun) crosses, carrying the great swelling passage of his course (πόρον [passage] is missing in Poet. scen. p. 105a) ουθεις (thus the Venice codex without accent) having escaped the holy darkness of black-horsed night.
having rushed through the swelling, swift-running passage
But do you wish to pluck the blood of your own brother?
the blood of a brother and of a common father.
the band of women, their own cousins.
to their close friends — their own cousins.
But the own cousins are nothing more than the cousins, but exactly the same.
self-sufficient, following one's own will, or, as Hermann interprets, acting on one's own impulse.

where the scholiast says: ἡ γὰρ νέα νηδὺς τῶν τέκνων ἑαυτῇ ἀρκεῖν καὶ βοηθεῖν βούλεται, ὅ ἐστιν ἀνύειν βούλεται τὰς ἐπιθυμίας [for the young belly of the children wishes to be sufficient and helpful to itself, that is, it wishes to accomplish its desires].
the young belly of the children is self-sufficient.
for the young belly of the children wishes to be sufficient and helpful to itself, that is, it wishes to accomplish its desires
But if again, which may it not happen, misfortune should befall.
one adorned with Persian robes, the other again with Dorian.
and again the night-wandering toil from battle arranges them.
some things one might say are easy to bear, others again blameless.
and again on land it was present.
now again be a savior and healer.
nor again will I liken them to Gorgon shapes.
for if —, but if again with the kindred children of Aegyptus your — through battle I will come to the end.
and she again, speaking ill-omened words, calls upon the god.
and again my dear heart is shaken.
see again, you who hear these evils, the device.
